transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I'm mainly here because my sleep has just gotten really unreliable lately. 

Even when I go to bed completely exhausted, I just lie there... replaying sales forecasts and issues with my team. And then, if I do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again. It's really starting to wear on me.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, not just work?

Yeah, I do. Most days, it feels like my mind just jumps from one thing to the next. I'll be worrying about whether we're going to hit our launch numbers, and then I'm suddenly stressing over whether someone on my team is about to quit. But it's not just the job—it spills over into other things, too, like the mortgage, or a client renewal. 

It's just... I don't know, it feels like every small delay or hiccup could turn into something major, no matter what part of my life it's about.
Did these sleep and worry problems start after a particular stressful event or change in your life?

Yeah, actually. It really started building since the sales division reorganization we had. That was... about thirteen months ago now. It just kind of kicked off around then and hasn't really let up since.
When you start worrying, do you find it hard to stop or control the worry?

Yeah, I really do. I'll try to reason with myself, you know? I'll literally tell myself, 'Brenda, you've done the plan, just let it go.' But it doesn't work. Maybe five minutes later, I'm right back in another loop. It's like I manage to check one concern off my list, only to have three more pop up right behind it. I just can't seem to turn it off once it starts.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?
No, not really. I mean, I feel exhausted and stressed out all the time, but I wouldn't say I feel depressed or down. It's really just the constant worrying that's getting to me.
For at least the past 6 months, have you been worrying like this on most days?

Yeah, definitely most days. Like I mentioned, it's been pretty constant since that reorganization over a year ago, so it's been way longer than six months. Most days, my mind just... jumps around. I'll be worrying about whether we're going to hit our launch numbers, and then suddenly I'm stressing over whether someone on my team is about to quit. Then it shifts to the mortgage, or, you know, an upcoming client renewal. It just feels like every small delay could turn into something major.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up?

Yeah, I do. I feel wound up almost all the time, actually. It's like... I feel like I'm sitting in a high-pressure pipeline review even when I'm just at home eating dinner. And physically, my shoulders just stay tight no matter how much I try to relax them.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

No, not really. I mean, even with all the worrying, I can still focus on my work when I need to. If I have to run a team meeting or go through a spreadsheet, I can pay attention just fine. So, no, I wouldn't say I've had any real trouble concentrating.
Do you get tired easily?

No, I haven't really noticed being easily tired. I mean, I work long hours, so I get tired at night like anyone else, but during the day... no, I wouldn't say I run out of energy easily or anything like that. If anything, I'm usually just running on nervous energy.
Do you often notice muscle tension?

Well, just what I mentioned a minute ago about my shoulders being tight. But other than that... no, I haven't really noticed my muscles aching or feeling tense anywhere else. It's pretty much just my shoulders.
When you’re lying awake at night, is your mind usually filled with worries?

Yeah, definitely. Most days, and especially at night, my mind just kind of jumps around. I'll start out worrying about whether we're going to hit our launch numbers at work, and then suddenly I'm stressing over whether someone on my team is about to quit. Then it shifts to the mortgage, or a client renewal... it just keeps going. It really feels like every small delay could turn into something major, and I just lie there thinking about it all.
On nights when you can’t sleep, is it because your mind is busy worrying?

Yeah, like I just mentioned, that's exactly it. It's the worrying that keeps me awake. My brain just won't shut off with all those work and mortgage things I was just talking about, so I just end up lying there unable to sleep.
Besides the sleep problem, has this constant worrying been causing problems for you during the day?

Yeah, it really has. It's started affecting both my work and my home life. At work, I spend so much time second-guessing my decisions that, well, my pipeline reviews end up running pretty tense. And then by the time I actually get home, I'm just completely drained. I end up being too reactive, and I'm just not fully present with my husband.
If your worrying were under control, do you think you would still have trouble sleeping?

I don't really know. I mean, I'd like to think I would sleep fine if my mind was just quiet. But honestly, it's been so long since I went to bed without all those thoughts running through my head... I'm not entirely sure.
Have you had nights where you couldn’t sleep even when you weren’t worrying about anything?

Not really. I mean, I can't even remember the last time I went to bed and wasn't worrying about something. It feels like the worrying is always there, so I haven't really had a night where my mind was totally clear but I still couldn't sleep.
